name: Giddel
overview: Giddel is a male servant of Solomon mentioned in the book of Ezra. His tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. He is identified primarily by his role as Solomon's servant, indicating a position of service during the time of Solomon's reign.
namesAndTitles: The name Giddel means 'big' according to the Hebrew origin noted in Ezra 2:56. This is the only name attributed to him in Scripture and does not carry a divine or symbolic title beyond its literal meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Giddel beyond his identification as Solomon's servant. No other familial or relational connections are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Giddel's significance lies in his service under Solomon, highlighting the presence of individuals who contributed to Solomon's household or administration. Though not extensively detailed, his mention underscores the broader community involved in the governance and service during Solomon's era as recorded in Ezra.
